key_insight: Cluster-weighted training focuses a deep surrogate model on high-error turbulence regimes, improving subgrid Reynolds-stress prediction over standard training.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more accurate data-driven path for subgrid-scale closure in solar turbulence simulations, with potential transfer to other regression-heavy multiscale flows.
method: Train MLP and 3D CNN surrogates on high-resolution StellarBox quiet-Sun simulations.
Use K-Means and Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering to identify error-prone regions.
Weight the loss by cluster-specific prediction errors to emphasize difficult cases.
evidence_signal: Compared with prior baselines, the clustered-loss CNN achieved 34% lower MSE and a higher R2 score across heights and depths in the solar atmosphere.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on the quality and stability of clustering, so cluster choice and weighting strategy need careful tuning to avoid biasing the model.
paper_title: Cluster-Weighted Training of Deep Surrogate Models for Subgrid Turbulent Transport
